scope: Calibration-aware DROID Strict-W novel-view generation lane
summary: The DROID-100 subset is synchronized but cannot support a calibrated wrist-to-exterior SOTA experiment; the new readiness gate blocks further raw-pixel VACE tuning.
evidence: The audit found both wrist and exterior RGB streams plus frame-aligned state/action/timestamps.

It also found unnamed motor channels and no camera serials, intrinsics, distortion, time-varying wrist extrinsics, exterior extrinsics, depth lineage, timestamp-offset evidence, or reviewed raw-DROID rights contract.
The persisted readiness result is BLOCKED rather than treating synchronized RGB as calibrated novel-view geometry.
lessons: Episode synchronization is necessary but not sufficient for geometric novel-view generation.
The current VACE wrist-pixel condition is in the wrong image coordinate system for an exterior target.
limitations: No GEN3C, TrajectoryCrafter, or ReCamMaster comparison can be claim-eligible without a target-camera contract.
The DROID-100 metadata does not identify the seven state/action channels beyond generic motor names.
next_actions: Acquire and rights-review raw DROID SVO/calibration/depth assets, then satisfy the Strict-W readiness contract before launching geometry-aware baselines.
